source.title: Uniform Manin-Mumford for a family of genus 2 curves
source.authors: Laura DeMarco, Holly Krieger and Hexi Ye
readSections: Entire arXiv v2 (3 December 2019, the latest and post-referee version), 49 pages: §§1–9 and references, read 2026-09-22 (PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/1901.09945v2, SHA-256 8fc51ac36f9fc4b406c7bb44cdeccf31386e81e0a471176a69e80a1a0766bab8). The typeset Annals PDF was not accessible, so the published version was not collated.

summary: Proves a uniform bound on common torsion images π(E_{t₁}^tors) ∩ π(E_{t₂}^tors) for two Legendre curves (Theorem 1.4), hence uniform Manin–Mumford at Weierstrass points for bielliptic genus-2 curves over ℂ (Theorem 1.1) and uniform Bogomolov for them over Q̄ (Theorem 1.9). The method bounds the Arakelov–Zhang pairing of the Lattès heights ĥ_{t₁}, ĥ_{t₂} from below, uniformly (Theorem 1.5) and linearly in the parameter height (Theorem 1.6). It uses nonarchimedean energy computations and archimedean estimates from degenerations in the hybrid space. It also bounds the pairing from above by quantitative equidistribution when the heights share many small points (Theorem 7.1). The atlas plans heights, Lattès canonical heights, Berkovich points, equidistribution, Manin–Mumford and Jacobians. It lacks Berkovich potential theory, the hybrid space, the Arakelov–Zhang pairing machinery and the uniform unlikely-intersection results. The independent review (REV-PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20) collated the published Annals version, which renumbers Theorems 1.4–1.9 as 1.5–1.10 and adds Propositions 8.3 and 9.2. It added four items and five further misprints or gaps (E9–E13), revised the corrections of E5 and E7, and confirmed that E7 is an error that needs its repair.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (uniform Manin–Mumford for bielliptic genus-2 curves)
items.statement: There is a uniform B such that |j_P(X) ∩ J(X)_tors| ≤ B for every smooth bielliptic curve X of genus 2 over ℂ and every Weierstrass point P of X, where j_P : X → J(X) is the Abel–Jacobi embedding based at P.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.1; proof §9.3, p.47, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Proposition 9.1 gives |j_Q(X) ∩ J_tors| ≤ 16|π₁(E₁^tors) ∩ π₂(E₂^tors)|, bounded by Corollary 8.2; other Weierstrass points differ from Q by 2-torsion. The bound is not explicit (Remark 1.2); Poonen and Stoll give examples with ≥ 22 and 34 points.

items.name: Manin–Mumford for curves (Raynaud)
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve X of genus ≥ 2 over ℂ and P ∈ X(ℂ), j_P(X) ∩ J(X)_tors is finite; more generally a curve of genus ≥ 2 in an abelian variety contains only finitely many torsion points (the form used after Conjecture 1.3).
items.locator: (1.1), p.1, citing Raynaud [Ra]; applied after Conjecture 1.3, p.2, to the lift of the diagonal in E₁ × E₂, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.5 plans Manin–Mumford with precise field hypotheses.

items.name: Legendre family and its standard projection
items.statement: E_t : y² = x(x − 1)(x − t) for t ∈ ℂ ∖ {0,1}, with the standard projection π(x,y) = x, a degree-two quotient identifying P and −P and branched exactly over π(E_t[2]) = {0, 1, t, ∞}; j(t) = 256(1 − t + t²)³/(t²(1 − t)²) (2.5).
items.note: Mathlib `WeierstrassCurve` covers E_t as the Weierstrass curve with a₂ = −(1+t), a₄ = t (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Weierstrass.lean); no Legendre-specific API is needed.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (common torsion images of two Legendre curves)
items.statement: There is a uniform B with |π(E_{t₁}^tors) ∩ π(E_{t₂}^tors)| ≤ B for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in ℂ ∖ {0,1}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p.3; proof §8.2, p.44, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019); published version (Ann. Math. 191 (2020)): Theorem 1.5, p.951
items.note: Over Q̄ from Theorem 8.1; over ℂ by specialization: if t₁ is transcendental, an algebraic common torsion image lies in π(E_t^tors) for all t (it is a root of a division polynomial with coefficients in ℚ[t]), and only 0, 1, ∞ do so [DWY, Prop. 1.4]; since 0, 1, ∞ are always common, N > B ≥ 3 common images force a transcendental one; the field ℚ(t₁, t₂, x₁, …, x_N) then has transcendence degree 1 and specializes to a Q̄-pair with as many common images.

items.name: Corollary 8.2 (the case |π₁(E₁[2]) ∩ π₂(E₂[2])| = 3 of the Bogomolov–Fu–Tschinkel conjecture)
items.statement: There is a uniform B with |π₁(E₁^tors) ∩ π₂(E₂^tors)| ≤ B for all elliptic curves E₁, E₂ over ℂ and standard projections π_i with |π₁(E₁[2]) ∩ π₂(E₂[2])| = 3.
items.locator: Corollary 8.2 and proof, pp.44–45; Conjecture 1.3, p.2, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019); published version: Corollary 8.2, pp.993–994, Conjecture 1.4, p.951
items.note: Move the three common branch values to {0,1,∞}, translate by 2-torsion so each π_i(O_i) = ∞, and put both curves in Legendre form. The full BFT conjecture (common branch set of any size < 4) stays open in this paper.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 (uniform positivity of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing)
items.statement: There is δ > 0 with ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≥ δ for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, p.4; proof §6.3, p.37, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (misprint E4); published version: Theorem 1.6, p.952, proof §6.3, p.986
items.note: If the pairing tends to 0, the archimedean local energies are small on places of total weight ≥ 1/2, forcing the parameters toward the diagonal or the cusps at places of weight ≥ 1/8; then h(s_n, t_n) → ∞, contradicting Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (the pairing grows with the parameter height)
items.statement: There are α, β > 0 with ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≥ α h(t₁, t₂) − β for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1}, h the naive height on 𝔸²(Q̄); one may take α = 1/512 (Remark 6.4).
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p.4; proof §6.2, pp.35–36, Remark 6.4, p.36, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019); published version: Theorem 1.7, p.952, proof §6.2, p.984
items.note: Lemma 6.2 applied to (t₁, t₂) and (1 − t₁, 1 − t₂), with Lemma 6.3: α = r/16 − r²/2 for 0 < r ≤ 1/16.

items.name: Proposition 1.8 (finiteness of joint small points)
items.statement: For 0 < b < δ/2 (δ of Theorem 1.5) the set S(b, t₁, t₂) = {x ∈ ℙ¹(Q̄) : ĥ_{t₁}(x) + ĥ_{t₂}(x) ≤ b} is finite for every t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.8, p.5; proof §6.4, p.38, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019); published version: Proposition 1.9, p.953
items.note: Zhang's essential-minimum inequality for the metric (‖·‖₁‖·‖₂)^{1/2}, whose self-pairing is ½ ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂}.

items.name: Theorem 1.9 (uniform Bogomolov for bielliptic genus-2 curves over Q̄)
items.statement: There are B and b > 0 with |{x ∈ j_P(X)(Q̄) : ĥ_{L_X}(x) ≤ b}| ≤ B for every smooth genus-2 curve X over Q̄ with a degree-two map to an elliptic curve and every Weierstrass point P, where L_X = Φ*L_D for the isogeny Φ : J(X) → E₁ × E₂ of Proposition 9.1 and D = {O₁} × E₂ + E₁ × {O₂}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.9, p.5; proof §9.4, p.47, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (the proof treats only P = Q, sourceIssues E8); published version: Theorem 1.10, p.953, proof §9.4, p.997
items.note: ĥ_{L_X} = ½(ĥ_{t₁} ∘ π ∘ Φ₁ + ĥ_{t₂} ∘ π ∘ Φ₂) by functoriality, and Theorem 8.1.

items.name: Logarithmic Weil height on ℙ¹(Q̄) and 𝔸²(Q̄)
items.statement: h : ℙ¹(Q̄) → ℝ, and the naive height h(t₁, t₂) on 𝔸²(Q̄), with 2h(x) = Σ_v r_v |log|x|_v| for x ≠ 0, r_v = [K_v:ℚ_v]/[K:ℚ].
items.note: Mathlib `Projectivization.logHeight` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Projectivization.lean:51) for fields with `Height.AdmissibleAbsValues`; the Q̄ extension is RP.0 work.

items.name: Néron–Tate height on E_t
items.statement: The canonical height ĥ_{E_t} on E_t(K), for K a number field, a quadratic form vanishing exactly on torsion.
items.locator: §2.1, p.6; §9.4, p.47, citing Silverman [Si], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Tau Ceti `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight` (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:124), with `canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder` (line 338) under a Northcott instance, over fields with `Height.AdmissibleAbsValues`.

items.name: The Lattès map f_t and the dynamical canonical height ĥ_t
items.statement: Multiplication by 2 on E_t descends through π to f_t(x) = (x² − t)²/(4x(x − 1)(x − t)) (2.1), of degree 4. The dynamical canonical height ĥ_t(x) = lim 4^{-n} h(f_t^n(x)) (2.2) satisfies ĥ_{E_t}(P) = ½ ĥ_t(π(P)), ĥ_t ≥ 0, and ĥ_t(x) = 0 iff x ∈ π(E_t^tors).
items.locator: §2.1, (2.1)–(2.2), pp.6–7, citing [Si], [CS], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (notation slip E1)
items.note: ArithmeticDynamics DY.1 plans canonical heights of polarized morphisms, with preperiodic points exactly the zeros, and multiplication on abelian varieties as an acceptance example.

items.name: Escape rates and local heights at every place
items.statement: For F_t(z,w) = ((z² − tw²)², 4zw(z − w)(z − tw)) and each place v, G_{F_t,v}(z,w) = lim 4^{-n} log ‖F_t^n(z,w)‖_v (2.3) and λ_{t,v}(x) = G_{F_t,v}(x,1) (2.4) give ĥ_t as the Galois-averaged sum of r_v λ_{t,v}; λ_{t,v} extends continuously to ℙ¹(ℂ_v) ∖ {∞} with λ_{t,v}(x) = log|x|_v + O(1), and Σ_v r_v c_v = 0 for its constant terms (2.6).
items.locator: §§2.1–2.2, (2.3)–(2.4), p.7; (2.6), p.10, citing Baker–Rumely [BR, Ch. 10], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (misprint E1)
items.note: DY.2 plans nonarchimedean escape rates; the archimedean escape rate and the global decomposition are routed to DY.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (symmetries of the Legendre escape rates)
items.locator: Proposition 2.1 and proof, pp.7–8, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Conjugation by A(z,w) = (w − z, w) and B(z,w) = (z, tw). Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: The Berkovich projective line over ℂ_v
items.statement: P^{1,an}_v: points of types I–IV, disks ζ_{a,r}, the Gauss point ζ_{0,1}, the hyperbolic metric d_hyp(ζ_{a,r₁}, ζ_{a,r₂}) = log(r₁/r₂) for r₁ ≥ r₂ > 0 on H = 𝔸^{1,an}_v ∖ ℂ_v, and interval measures; P^{1,an}_v = ℙ¹(ℂ) at archimedean v.
items.locator: §2.3, pp.8–9, citing Baker–Rumely [BR], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0–TB.1 plan Berkovich spectra, the four point types on the affine line and the hyperbolic metric. Type II points are the ζ_{a,r} with r in the value group |ℂ_v^×|_v, type III those with r outside it (the paper says 'rational' and 'irrational', sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Potential theory on the Berkovich line
items.statement: The (distribution-valued) Laplacian on P^{1,an}_v normalized by Δ log⁺|z|_v = ω_v − δ_∞ (ω_v the circle measure or the Gauss point mass); measures with continuous potentials; the Hsia kernel and the mutual energy (ν₁, ν₂)_v (2.13)–(2.14), with (ν₁, ν₂)_v = −∫g₁ dν₂ for mass-zero measures with continuous potentials, and (ν, ν)_v ≥ 0 with equality iff ν = 0 ([FRL1, Props. 2.6, 4.5]).
items.locator: §2.3, p.8; §2.7, (2.13)–(2.15), p.12, citing [BR, Chs. 4–5] and Favre–Rivera-Letelier [FRL1, §4.4], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (misprint E9)
items.note: Routed to TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.1/TB.6 as a source. The paper prints the positivity as '(ν₁, ν₂)_v ≥ 0 with equality if and only if ν₁ = ν₂' (misprint E9); the statement above is the intended one.

items.name: Canonical measures of the Lattès maps
items.statement: Δλ_{t,v} = µ_{t,v} − δ_∞, where µ_{t,v} is the canonical measure of f_t at v, supported on its Julia set; at archimedean v it is the maximal-entropy measure π_*(Haar on E_t(ℂ)); at finite v with good reduction it is δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, and f_t has potential good reduction iff µ_{t,v} is a point mass at a type II point iff |j(t)|_v ≤ 1.
items.locator: §2.4, p.9, citing [FRL1], [BR, Thm. 10.2], Baker–Petsche [BPe, Thm. 1], Milnor [Mi], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.2 (local dynamics and reduction) as a source.

items.name: Adelic metrics on O_{ℙ¹}(1) and heights from adelic measures
items.statement: A continuous semipositive adelic metric on O(1) (Zhang) gives a height; ĥ_t comes from the metric −log‖s(z)‖_{t,v} = λ_{t,v}(z). Conversely a collection of probability measures {µ_v} with continuous potentials, equal to ω_v at almost all places, determines such a metric, unique up to factors e^{c_v} with Σ_v r_v c_v = 0, and hence a unique height normalized by h · h = 0 ([FRL1]).
items.locator: §2.5, pp.9–10; §2.8, pp.12–13, citing Zhang [Zh2] and [FRL1], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.4 as a source.

items.name: The Arakelov–Zhang pairing and local energies
items.statement: For heights from adelic metrics, ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} := ĥ_{t₁}((u)) + ĥ_{t₂}((s)) + Σ_v r_v ∫ log‖s‖^{-1}_{t₁,v} Δ(log‖u‖^{-1}_{t₂,v}) (2.9), independent of s, u; it equals Σ_v r_v E_v(t₁, t₂) with local energy E_v = ½(∫(λ_{t₁,v} − λ_{t₂,v}) dµ_{t₂,v} + ∫(λ_{t₂,v} − λ_{t₁,v}) dµ_{t₁,v}) = ½(µ_{t₁,v} − µ_{t₂,v}, µ_{t₁,v} − µ_{t₂,v})_v ≥ 0, with equality iff µ_{t₁,v} = µ_{t₂,v} (Proposition 2.2); E_v(s,t) is continuous in (s,t) and, at archimedean v, vanishes iff s = t (used in the proof of Theorem 1.5, p.37); ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≥ 0 with equality iff t₁ = t₂ (2.7)–(2.8) [PST].
items.locator: §2.6, (2.7)–(2.12), Proposition 2.2, pp.10–11; (2.15), p.12; §2.8, p.13, citing Zhang [Zh2], Chambert-Loir [CL2], Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker [PST], [FRL1], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.4 ("construct the dynamical energy") as a source. The paper's justification of (2.7) argues only that the measures determine the height; the converse it needs follows from equidistribution (1.3) or from [PST] (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Proposition 2.3 (symmetry of the local energy)
items.statement: E_v(t₂, t₁) = E_v(t₁, t₂) = E_v(1 − t₁, 1 − t₂) = E_v(1/t₁, 1/t₂).
items.locator: Proposition 2.3 and proof, p.11, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Fili's metric on adelic heights
items.statement: For normalized heights from continuous semipositive adelic metrics on O(1), h₁ · h₂ = ½ Σ_v r_v (µ_{1,v} − µ_{2,v}, µ_{1,v} − µ_{2,v})_v, and dist(h₁, h₂) = (h₁ · h₂)^{1/2} is a metric; in particular (h₁ · h₂)^{1/2} ≤ (h₁ · h₃)^{1/2} + (h₂ · h₃)^{1/2} (7.3).
items.locator: §2.8, pp.12–13; (7.3), p.39, citing Fili [Fi, Thm. 1], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.4 as a source.

items.name: Arithmetic equidistribution for adelic heights on ℙ¹
items.statement: For heights h₁, h₂ from continuous semipositive adelic metrics on O_{ℙ¹}(1), normalized by h_i · h_i = 0: if x_n ∈ ℙ¹(Q̄) are distinct with h₁(x_n) → 0, then h₂(x_n) → h₁ · h₂ (1.3).
items.locator: (1.3), p.3, citing Chambert-Loir [CL1], [FRL1], Baker–Rumely [BR], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: ArithmeticDynamics DY.4 plans a primary equidistribution theorem for semipositive adelic metrized line bundles.

items.name: Zhang's essential-minimum inequality
items.statement: For a semipositive adelically metrized line bundle L̄ on ℙ¹, liminf h_{L̄}(x_n) ≥ (L̄ · L̄)/(2 deg L) along any sequence of distinct points of ℙ¹(Q̄) ([Zh2, Thm. 1.10]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.8, p.38, citing Zhang [Zh2, Thm. 1.10], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.4 as a source.

items.name: Product formula for the energy of a finite set
items.statement: For a finite set F ⊂ K, Σ_v r_v ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = 0, where [F]_v is the uniform probability measure on F ⊂ ℂ_v (2.16).
items.locator: (2.16), p.12, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (sign misprint E2)
items.note: Routed to DY.4 with the quantitative-equidistribution tools.

items.name: Theorem 3.1 (nonarchimedean energy lower bound)
items.statement: For finite v and t₁, t₂ ∈ K ∖ {0,1}: E_v(t₁, t₂) − (4/3) log|2|_v ≥ log²|t₁/t₂|_v / (6 log max{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v}) if both |t_i|_v > 1; ≥ log²|t₁/t₂|_v / (−6 log min{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v}) if both < 1; and ≥ |log|t₁/t₂|_v|/6 otherwise. Equality holds for v ∤ 2 with min{|t₁ − 1|_v, |t₂ − 1|_v} ≥ 1.
items.locator: Theorem 3.1, p.13; proof §§3.2, 3.4, pp.15–18, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Direct integration of the explicit potentials against interval measures. Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 3.2–3.4 (canonical measure and escape rate at v ∤ 2)
items.statement: For v ∤ 2, f_t has good reduction iff |t(t − 1)|_v = 1; otherwise it has no potential good reduction and µ_{t,v} is the interval measure on [ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{0,|t|_v}] (|t|_v ≠ 1) or [ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{1,|1−t|_v}] (|1 − t|_v < 1), f_t acting on it by a tent map. The escape rate G_{F_t,v}(z,1) is given explicitly by (3.1) for |t(t − 1)|_v ≥ 1 (Proposition 3.3) and (3.3) for |t|_v < 1.
items.locator: Propositions 3.2–3.4 and proofs, pp.13–15, citing Favre–Rivera-Letelier [FRL2, §5.1], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 3.5–3.6 (canonical measure and escape rate at v | 2)
items.statement: For v | 2, µ_{t,v} is the interval measure on [ζ_{0,|t/4|}, ζ_{0,|4|}] for |t|_v < |16|_v, on [ζ_{0,1/|4|}, ζ_{0,|4t|}] for |t|_v > 1/|16|_v and on [ζ_{1,|1−t|/|4|}, ζ_{1,|4|}] for |1 − t|_v < |16|_v; for |16|_v ≤ |t|_v ≤ 1/|16|_v with |1 − t|_v ≥ |16|_v, f_t has potential good reduction and µ_{t,v} is a point mass in H. The escape rate is given by (3.4) for |t|_v ≥ 1/|16|_v and by (3.5) for |t|_v ≤ |16|_v; the middle range of (3.5) should read |t/4|_v < |z|_v < |4|_v (misprint E12).
items.locator: Propositions 3.5–3.6 and proofs, pp.16–17, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (misprint E12)
items.note: The support point in the potentially good range is not computed in the paper. Its diameter is |Δ_t|_v^{1/6} = |2|_v^{2/3}|t(t − 1)|_v^{1/3} (a change of coordinates x = u²x′ + r to a good model has |u|¹² = |Δ_t|, and the resultant of f_t is Δ_t²), which is < 1 when |t(t − 1)|_v < |2|_v^{−2}; its centre can be taken to be any 3-torsion x-coordinate (sourceIssues E7). Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: The hybrid space of a degenerating family
items.statement: For X = 𝔻* × ℙ¹(ℂ), the hybrid space X^hyb replaces the central fibre by the Berkovich line P^{1,an}_{k₀} over k₀ = ℂ((T)), with the Boucksom–Jonsson topology: annular sets {|t|^{a+δ} < |z| < |t|^{a−δ}, 0 < |t| < δ} ∪ A(|T|₀^{a+δ}, |T|₀^{a−δ}) and the disk-like sets are open, and the topology on the central fibre is the Berkovich topology.
items.locator: §4 intro, p.18; proof of Proposition 4.2, pp.21–22, citing Boucksom–Jonsson [BJ, §2.2, Def. 4.9], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 (Berkovich spectra of Banach rings) as a source.

items.name: Degeneration of the measures of maximal entropy (DeMarco–Faber, Favre)
items.statement: As t → 0, µ_t(A_t(a, b, C)) → length([0,1] ∩ [b, a]) for the annuli A_t(a,b,C) = {C^{-1}|t|^a ≤ |z| ≤ C|t|^b} with C > 1 and real a ≥ b (4.3), and µ_t → µ̂_f weakly in X^hyb; the normalized potentials ϕ(t, z) = Φ_t(z)/log|t|^{-1}, with Φ_t = G_{F_t}(·,1) − log⁺|·|, extend continuously to X^hyb with central values the explicit potential φ̂_f (4.8) of µ̂_f − ω₀.
items.locator: §§4.1–4.3, (4.2)–(4.8), pp.19–21, citing DeMarco–Faber [DF1, Thm. B], [DF2, Thm. D] and Favre [Fa, Thm. B, Thm. 2.10, §4.3], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019) (misprint E3 in (4.1))
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.6 (families) as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.1 and (4.4) (equidistribution on annuli near a cusp)
items.statement: For ε > 0 and n ≥ 1 there is δ > 0 with 1/n − ε < µ_t({|t|^{(i+1)/n} ≤ |z| ≤ |t|^{i/n}}) < 1/n + ε for 0 < |t| < δ and 0 ≤ i < n; hence µ_t({|z| ≥ 1} ∪ {|z| ≤ |t|}) < 1/n.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1 and (4.4), p.20, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 4.2–4.3 (uniform continuity of potentials near a cusp)
items.statement: For ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |ϕ(t,z) − φ̂_f(ζ_{0,|T|₀^a})| < ε for 0 < |t| < δ, all a ∈ ℝ and |log|z|/log|t| − a| < δ; similarly, given also M > 1 (with δ depending on M), |G_{F_t}(z,1)/log|t|^{-1} − ĝ_f(ζ_{0,|T|₀^a})| < ε for |z| ≤ M.
items.locator: Propositions 4.2–4.3 and proof, pp.21–22, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Compactness of the segment [0,∞] in P^{1,an}_{k₀} and the hybrid topology. Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.4 (regularizing finite sets)
items.statement: For ε > 0 there is c(ε) > 0 with |(µ_t, [F]) − (µ_t, [F]_r)| < ε max{log|t|^{-1}, log|t − 1|^{-1}, log|t|, 1} for all t ∈ ℂ ∖ {0,1}, every finite F ⊂ ℂ and every r ≤ c min{|t|², |t − 1|², |t|^{-2}}, where [F]_r spreads [F] uniformly on circles of radius r.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (archimedean energy, one escaping parameter)
items.statement: For ε > 0 and compact C ⊂ ℂ ∖ {0,1} there is δ > 0 with (1/6 − ε) log|s|^{-1} ≤ E_∞(s,t) ≤ (1/6 + ε) log|s|^{-1} for 0 < |s| < δ and t ∈ C.

items.name: Theorems 5.2, 5.4 and Proposition 5.3 (both parameters at the same cusp)

For b ≤ B the error is uniform: (E₀(µ̂₁, µ̂_b) ± ε) log|t|^{-1} with E₀(µ̂₁, µ̂_b) = (b − 1)²/(6b).

items.statement: For 0 < r ≤ 1/16 there is C₀ with 6E_v(t₁,t₂) ≥ (3r/4)|log|t₁/t₂|_v| − C₀ at every archimedean v where |log|t₂/t₁|_v| ≥ r max{|log|t₁|_v|, |log|t₂|_v|}.

items.statement: For a rational map g : ℙⁿ ⇢ ℙᵐ of degree d, h(g(P)) ≤ d h(P) + C off the indeterminacy locus ([HS, Thm. B.2.5]).

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (a birational height comparison)
items.statement: There is C with h(t₂/t₁, (1 − t₂)/(1 − t₁)) ≥ ½ h(t₁,t₂) − C for t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1}.
items.locator: Lemma 6.3 and proof, pp.35–36, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)

items.name: Heights attached to a regularized finite set
items.statement: For a Galois-stable finite F ⊂ K̄ and radii η = {η_v} (η_v = 1 for almost all v), the adelic measure m_{F,η} (uniform on circles of radius η_v about F at archimedean v; uniform on the points ζ_{x,η_v}, x ∈ F, counted with multiplicity, at finite v) defines a height h_{F,η} with h_{F,η} · h_{F,η} = 0 (7.2) and local heights α_v + |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log max{|z − x|_v, η_v}; moreover (m_{F,η,v}, m_{F,η,v})_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log η_v)/|F| ([FRL1, Lemma 4.11], [Fi, Lemma 12]).

items.statement: For 0 ≤ b < δ/2 and ε > 0 there is C(ε) with ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≤ 4b + (ε + C(ε)/|S(b,t₁,t₂)|)(h(t₁,t₂) + 1) for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1}; the case b = 0 is Theorem 1.7 with |S(0,t₁,t₂)| = N(t₁,t₂) = |π(E_{t₁}^tors) ∩ π(E_{t₂}^tors)|.

items.name: Division polynomials over a polynomial base
items.statement: The division polynomials of E_t have coefficients in ℚ[t], so the torsion images π(E_t[n]) are cut out by polynomials in (x, t).
items.locator: §8.2, p.44, citing Silverman [Si, Ex. 3.7], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)

items.name: Torsion images common to all Legendre curves (DeMarco–Wang–Ye)
items.statement: The only x ∈ ℙ¹(ℂ) with x ∈ π(E_t^tors) for all t ∈ ℂ ∖ {0,1} are 0, 1, ∞ ([DWY, Prop. 1.4]).
items.locator: §8.2, p.44, citing [DWY, Prop. 1.4], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 9.1 (bielliptic genus-2 curves as lifts of the diagonal)
items.statement: Every genus-2 curve X admitting a degree-two map to an elliptic curve (the surface L₂ ⊂ M₂, Jacobians with real multiplication by the order of discriminant 4) has a model y² = x⁶ − s₁x⁴ + s₂x² − 1 and is the normalization of the lift of the diagonal D ⊂ ℙ¹ × ℙ¹ under standard projections π₁ × π₂ of elliptic curves E₁, E₂ with |π₁(E₁[2]) ∩ π₂(E₂[2])| = 3; the group laws on E_i are taken with origin O_i over a common branch value r, with Π(ν(Q)) = (r, r), and there are a Weierstrass point Q and a degree-4 isogeny Φ : J(X) → E₁ × E₂ with Φ ∘ j_Q(X) = (π₁ × π₂)^{-1}(D).
items.locator: §§9.1–9.2, Proposition 9.1 and proof, pp.45–47, citing Shaska–Völklein [SV], Jacobi [Ja], McMullen [Mc, Thm. 4.10], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: The three nontrivial elements of ker Φ are the differences of the two Weierstrass points over each common branch value. The Jacobi model is cited from [SV]/[Ja], not proved. Routed to the uniformity Part II with Theorems 1.1 and 1.9.

items.name: Riemann–Hurwitz formula
items.statement: For a finite separable morphism of smooth projective curves, 2g(X) − 2 = deg(φ)(2g(Y) − 2) + deg R; used to see that the lift of the diagonal has genus 2.
items.locator: §9.1, p.45, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves layer 7 plans the different and the Hurwitz genus formula.

items.name: Jacobian and Abel–Jacobi embedding of a genus-2 curve
items.statement: J(X) and j_P : X → J(X), x ↦ [x − P]; differences of Weierstrass points are 2-torsion.
items.locator: §1, p.1; §9, pp.45–47, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layers D–F plan the Jacobian scheme, abelian varieties and the Abel–Jacobi map with its universal property.

items.name: Néron–Tate heights on abelian varieties and their functoriality
items.statement: For a symmetric ample line bundle L on an abelian variety A over Q̄, the Néron–Tate height ĥ_L is a quadratic form, vanishing on torsion, with ĥ_L(x + T) = ĥ_L(x) for torsion T. For a homomorphism Φ of abelian varieties, ĥ_{Φ*L} = ĥ_L ∘ Φ; on E₁ × E₂ with D = {O₁} × E₂ + E₁ × {O₂}, ĥ_{L_D}(P₁,P₂) = ĥ_{E₁}(P₁) + ĥ_{E₂}(P₂), where ĥ_{E_i} is the height for the divisor (O_i), i.e. ½ ĥ_{t_i} ∘ π in Legendre form ([HS, Thm. B.5.6]).
items.locator: §9.4, p.47, citing Hindry–Silverman [HS, Thm. B.5.6], arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0 plans Néron–Tate heights on abelian varieties with pullback laws. The translation invariance is what the correction of E8 uses.

items.name: Standard projections of elliptic curves
items.statement: A standard projection of an elliptic curve E over ℂ is any degree-two quotient π : E → ℙ¹ identifying P and −P; it has simple critical points at E[2]. For e ∈ E[2], π^e(P) = π(P + e) is again a standard projection, with π^e(E^tors) = π(E^tors).
items.locator: §1, p.2; proof of Corollary 8.2, pp.44–45; §9.1, p.45, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019); published version pp.950–951, 994–995
items.note: Added by the review: Corollary 8.2 and Proposition 9.1 use standard projections of arbitrary elliptic curves, not only the Legendre x-projection of item 3. Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.6 with Corollary 8.2.

items.name: Hyperelliptic involution and Weierstrass points of a genus-2 curve
items.statement: A genus-2 curve X is hyperelliptic; its hyperelliptic involution is the deck involution of the canonical degree-two map to ℙ¹, and its six Weierstrass points are the fixed points (the ramification points), whose pairwise differences are 2-torsion in J(X).
items.locator: §1, p.1; proof of Proposition 9.1, pp.46–47, arXiv v2 (3 December 2019)
items.note: Added by the review. Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves layer 10 plans hyperelliptic function fields (every genus-2 function field is hyperelliptic, with its models and ramified places) and layer 11 plans Weierstrass points and the hyperelliptic involution.

items.name: Proposition 8.3 (no uniform bound on the order of common torsion images; published version only)
items.statement: For every N > 0 and every x₀ ∈ Q̄ ∖ {0,1} there are t₁ ≠ t₂ in Q̄ ∖ {0,1} such that the points P_i = (x₀, ±√(x₀(x₀ − 1)(x₀ − t_i))) are torsion on E_{t_i} of order ≥ N, i = 1, 2.
items.locator: Proposition 8.3 and proof, §8.4, p.994 of the published version (Ann. Math. 191 (2020)); not in arXiv v2

items.name: Proposition 9.2 (no uniform bound on the torsion order for bielliptic genus-2 curves; published version only)
items.statement: For every N > 0 there are a curve X ∈ L₂ defined over Q̄ and a Weierstrass point P ∈ X such that j_P(X) ∩ J(X)^tors contains a point of order ≥ N.
items.locator: Proposition 9.2 and proof, §9.5, p.997, and Remark 1.3, p.950, of the published version (Ann. Math. 191 (2020)); not in arXiv v2

routes.reason: DY.2 owns local dynamics, escape rates and reduction, DY.4 equidistribution with the dynamical energy on adelic heights, and DY.6 families and proven unlikely-intersection cases as source-bound endpoints, with Lattès examples required. The paper is a source for all three layers. For DY.2 it supplies the escape rates at every place and the canonical measures of the Lattès maps. For DY.4 it supplies adelic metrics, the Arakelov–Zhang pairing, Fili's metric, Zhang's essential-minimum inequality and the regularized finite-set heights. For DY.6 its core theorems (the local energy estimates, Theorems 1.4–1.8, 7.1 and 8.1, and the hybrid-space degeneration estimates) are exactly the unlikely-intersection endpoint that layer asks for: uniformly bounded common torsion images for pairs of Lattès maps.

TB.0 owns Berkovich spectra of Banach rings, TB.1 the tree structure of the Berkovich line, and TB.6 measures and local heights. The paper needs Baker–Rumely potential theory on the Berkovich line (the Laplacian, the Hsia kernel and mutual energy with its positivity) and the Boucksom–Jonsson hybrid space of a degenerating family. These are analytic foundations that the atlas does not yet plan.

routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-YUAN-26, PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 under the same id, and their briefs remain binding. This paper contributes an early explicit family where uniform Manin–Mumford and uniform Bogomolov were proved by arithmetic dynamics. Import the Lattès heights, the Arakelov–Zhang pairing and the uniform common-torsion bound for Legendre curves (Theorems 1.4 and 8.1, Corollary 8.2) from ArithmeticDynamics DY.6, the Jacobian and Abel–Jacobi map from Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge D–F, and Néron–Tate functoriality from HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0. State and prove, as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye (Ann. Math. 191 (2020)), three results. Proposition 9.1: every bielliptic genus-2 curve (Jacobi model y² = x⁶ − s₁x⁴ + s₂x² − 1) normalizes the lift of the diagonal under π₁ × π₂ with three common branch values, and j_Q followed by a degree-4 isogeny J(X) → E₁ × E₂ lands on that lift. Theorem 1.1: |j_P(X) ∩ J(X)_tors| ≤ B uniformly for Weierstrass P. Theorem 1.9: uniform Bogomolov for L_X = Φ*L_D, treating every Weierstrass point by translation by 2-torsion (sourceIssues E8). Also state Proposition 9.2 of the published version: the order of the torsion points in Theorem 1.1 is not uniformly bounded. The published version numbers Theorem 1.9 as Theorem 1.10. Import hyperelliptic curves and Weierstrass points from Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves layers 10–11. Acceptance: both results are special cases of the uniform Manin–Mumford and Bogomolov bounds already in this Part II (Kühne; Gao–Ge–Kühne), and the DKY statement must follow from them; Stoll's curve with 34 torsion points shows B ≥ 34.
